post_title: How many first-place votes will the winner of the 2026 National League MVP Award receive?

question.title: How many first-place votes will the winner of the 2026 National League MVP Award receive?
question.description:
## How the NL MVP is voted
The National League MVP is awarded by the Baseball Writers' Association of America. Per the BBWAA's [Voting FAQ](https://bbwaa.com/voting-faq), two writers from each MLB city vote for each league's award — 30 voters for the NL — and each MVP ballot lists 10 players, tabulated at 14 points for first place, 9 for second, 8 for third, down to 1 for 10th. Ballots are submitted before the postseason begins and the results are embargoed until the televised announcement; the BBWAA then publishes the award release and a full ballot-by-ballot breakdown (e.g. the [2025 NL MVP ballots](https://bbwaa.com/25-nl-mvp-ballots)). The winner's first-place vote count is therefore a secret until announcement night, even though the ballots themselves were cast in late September/early October.

## 2026 awards calendar
The BBWAA finalists will be announced on MLB Network on Nov. 2, 2026. Rookie of the Year follows on Nov. 9, Manager of the Year on Nov. 10, and Cy Young on Nov. 11. The NL and AL MVP awards are the last BBWAA awards, announced live on MLB Network at 6 p.m. CT on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026 — the only major award inside this question's window.

## State of the NL race (as of Oct. 30, 2026)
Pete Crow-Armstrong (Cubs) is the clear frontrunner. In MLB.com's final 2026 MVP poll (Sept. 22, 38 voters), Crow-Armstrong received every first-place vote cast (38) and 190 total points, after taking the top spot from Shohei Ohtani in the Aug. 25 poll (29 of 37 first-place votes). He tied Kyle Schwarber (Phillies) for the MLB home-run lead with 45 and led MLB in WAR; MLB.com's season-ending stat-leaders piece called him "the surefire 2026 NL MVP." Ohtani, the 2021–2025 NL MVP (unanimous in 2023, 2024 and 2025), did not pitch in 2026 per MLB.com's poll write-ups. In the AL, Yordan Alvarez is an overwhelming favorite, so the open question on the NL side is not so much who wins as how close to unanimous the winner is.

## Why the vote count is not automatic
Recent NL MVP winners' first-place counts from the 30-person panel: 2019 Cody Bellinger 19, 2020 Freddie Freeman 28, 2021 Bryce Harper 17, 2022 Paul Goldschmidt 22, 2023 Ronald Acuña Jr. 30, 2024 Ohtani 30, 2025 Ohtani 30. Even strong favorites sometimes lose a handful of first-place votes to a rival with a compelling narrative (a 45-homer rival, a pitcher, or a player from a division winner), while genuine runaway seasons have produced sweeps in three straight years. Whether Crow-Armstrong or another winner lands at 30, 27 or lower depends on how roughly 30 beat writers weigh his power/WAR season against the rest of the field — an assessment MLB.com's panel of 38 experts is not identical to.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of first-place votes received by the winner of the 2026 National League [Most Valuable Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Most_Valuable_Player_Award), as reported in the BBWAA's official voting results published at https://bbwaa.com/ (the 2026 NL MVP release and its ballot-by-ballot breakdown). The award is announced live on MLB Network on November 12, 2026, and the count is the number of the 30 National League ballots — two BBWAA writers from each of the 15 NL cities — on which the winner is listed in first place. For scale, Shohei Ohtani received 30 first-place votes in the 2025 NL MVP balloting (https://bbwaa.com/25-nl-mvp-ballots) and Paul Goldschmidt received 22 in 2022, so a unanimous winner resolves as 30. If the BBWAA page is unavailable or its ballot breakdown is never published, the official first-place vote totals reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: If the BBWAA declares co-winners because two players tie in total voting points (as happened in the 1979 NL vote), the question resolves on the higher first-place vote total among those co-winners.
